display.title: Episode 436: Rabbi Akiva's Negel Vasser and the Drunken Father (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: A Three Weeks show: join Hashem's army and defeat the yetzer hara, Rabbi Akiva saved by washing negel vasser in prison, and the sad story of Naftali's drunken father.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during the Three Weeks of 5750. Uncle Yossi invites every child to join Tzivos Hashem by letter, describes the ID card, emblem and wallet members receive, and explains that Torah and mitzvos are the secret weapon that defeats the yetzer hara before Moshiach comes. A brother and sister recite the Shema in Studio 604; she says one of the Twelve Pesukim and he recites a Mishnah from Brachos. After tzedakah, story time tells how Rabbi Akiva, jailed for teaching Torah and given water after three days without any, used it to wash negel vasser; the amazed ruler freed him and made him an advisor. Uncle Yossi explains Rabbi Akiva's great rule, 'love your fellow as yourself', and the Alter Rebbe's teaching that love of every Jew leads to love of Hashem, which matters most in the Three Weeks. A story 'with no happy ending' follows: Naftali shows his drinking father a drunk lying in the street, but his father only asks where to get such a good drink. As in Parshas Acharei, we see others' ways only to know not to copy them. The show ends with candle-lighting times and a sponsor.
display.lesson: Love every Jew as yourself, and be an example of Torah living rather than copying the ways of others.

date.note: Said to be during the Three Weeks; candle time 8:05 PM fits mid-late July; one week after episode 435 (17 Tammuz 5750).

advisories.note: Rabbi Akiva is jailed for teaching Torah and left without food or water for three days.
A father's drinking problem; his son cries about it.
The Naftali story deliberately ends without the father changing.
Mentions that the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed for lack of Ahavas Yisroel.

privacy.note: A brother and sister named as Shema guests.

sources_cited.note: Rabbi Akiva's sayings, including that 'love your fellow as yourself' is a great rule of the Torah.
Parshas Acharei: do not follow the ways of Egypt and Canaan.
The Alter Rebbe: Ahavas Yisroel leads to Ahavas Hashem.

segments.title: Love Your Fellow as Yourself

segments.title: The Drunken Father
segments.summary: Naftali shows his drinking father a drunk in the street, hoping to shame him, but the father only asks where to get such a good drink.

segments.title: The lesson from Parshas Acharei
segments.summary: We are shown others' ways only so we know not to follow them; in the Three Weeks, be an example of Torah and peace.

relations.note: Episode 184 has the same join-Tzivos-Hashem talk, Rabbi Akiva story and Naftali story; the Shema guests differ.
The Naftali (Drunken Father) story first aired in episode 21.
Same story, another telling: 'Tanya Shiur 41 (Continued): End of Tanya Chapter 29, Rebuking the Yetzer Hara' (Stories, 43:02-44:30), told by Rabbi Yosef Goldstein (Uncle Yossi).

quality.notes: Largely a rebroadcast of episode 184 with new Shema guests. Suggest a parent note on the alcohol theme. Sponsor and candle times are period pieces.
